'''Peter Vincent Ridd''' is an Australian [[physicist]], author, and former professor at [[James Cook University]] (JCU), North Queensland, Australia.

Ridd is known for a lengthy legal battle with his former employer JCU, which has been variously characterised as a battle for [[academic freedom]]<ref>{{cite web | title=The High Court's defence of Academic Freedom in Ridd v JCU | url=https://www.auspublaw.org/blog/2021/11/the-high-courts-defence-of-academic-freedom-in-ridd-v-jcu }}</ref> and as a media campaign [[Climate change denial|seeking to discredit]] the science informing the protection of the [[Great Barrier Reef]].<ref>Konkes, C., & Foxwell-Norton, K. (2021). Science communication and mediatised environmental conflict: A cautionary tale. ''Public Understanding of Science'', ''30''(4), 470-483.</ref><ref>Foxwell-Norton, K., & Konkes, C. (2021). Climate change and the Great Barrier Reef: Environmental protest, climate science, and new/s media. In ''Climate Change and Journalism'' (pp. 103-120). Routledge.</ref><ref>Grien, A., & MacNeil, R. (2022). The role of journalistic voice in communicating climate scepticism. ''Public Understanding of Science'', ''31''(5), 563-571.</ref>

==Education ==
Ridd received a Bachelor of Science degree in Physics from [[James Cook University]] in 1978, and later a PhD in Physics from that same institution in 1980.<ref name =court2019>[https://platogbr.files.wordpress.com/2019/09/ridd-v-james-cook-university-no.2-2019-fcca-2489.pdf RIDD v JAMES COOK UNIVERSITY (No.2) &#91;2019&#93; FCCA 2489] Federal Circuit Court of Australia, 2019. "Dr Ridd was disciplined for repeated breaches of the same directions given to him over a course of almost two years. Dr Ridd was invited to remove confidential information he placed publicly online, and he refused to do so."</ref> At this time, he also joined the [[Australian Institute of Marine Science]]. He started studying the [[Great Barrier Reef]] in 1984, mainly focusing on [[ocean current]]s and the movement of [[sediment]].<ref>{{Citation|title=Peter Ridd's Fight for Freedom of Speech on Climate Change| date=18 March 2019 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QbKa015q4cI|via =[[YouTube]] |language=en|access-date=2021-10-21}}</ref>{{better source needed|date=March 2022}}

== Career ==
While teaching at JCU, Ridd was the head of the Physics department from 2009 to 2016, and head of the Marine Geophysical Laboratory at that institution for 15 years.<ref name =court2019/><ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.afr.com/policy/health-and-education/judge-vasta-to-proceed-with-existing-cases-20190722-p529ik|work=[[Australian Financial Review]]|title=Judge Vasta to proceed with existing cases|accessdate=2 January 2020 |first=Robert|last=Bolton|date=22 July 2019}}</ref>

===Great Barrier Reef article ===

With Piers Larcombe, Ridd wrote an [[opinion piece]] in November 2017, published in the January 2018 issue of ''[[The Marine Pollution Bulletin|Marine Pollution Bulletin]]'', challenging the prevailing understanding of the state of the [[Great Barrier Reef]], drawing attention to what he argued was a [[reproducibility crisis]] and certain specific papers relating to the state of the Great Barrier Reef, and recommending a new review body for [[policy science]].<ref name="MPB 201801" /> A viewpoint article in rebuttal was printed in the April 2018 issue of the same journal by Schaffelke ''et al.''<ref name="MPB 201804" /> Ridd replied in a further article in the June 2019 issue.<ref name="MPB 201906" />

===Dismissal from JCU ===

Beginning in April 2016, James Cook University took a number of disciplinary measures over two years against Ridd, which culminated in Ridd being fired, for refusing to take down confidential information which he had placed publicly online.<ref name =court2019/> The university denied that the dismissal was over Ridd's views on climate change.<ref name="Guardian 201806" /> Ridd filed two [[crowdfund]]ed lawsuits, the second over the dismissal.

On 16 April 2019, Ridd initially won the lawsuit,<ref name="Guardian 201909" /> with James Cook University found to be in violation of the ''[[Fair Work Act 2009]]''; in September 2019, Ridd was awarded in excess of AU$1 million, together with AU$125,000 pecuniary penalty. While the two parties continue to disagree whether the case related to academic freedom, the ruling judge said the case was "purely and simply about the proper construction of a clause in an enterprise agreement",<ref name="Guardian 201909" /> although he also stated James Cook University had "not understood the whole concept of intellectual freedom".<ref name="ABC 201904" /> In July 2020, JCU won an appeal against this judgement from the full bench of the [[Federal Court of Australia|Federal Court]].<ref>{{Cite web| last=Nothling| first=Lily|date =2020-07-22| title=University wins appeal over controversial academic's unfair sacking verdict |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-07-22/james-cook-university-can-appeal-unfair-sacking-of-peter-ridd/12481974|access-date=2020-07-22|website=ABC News|language=en-AU}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://sterlinglawqld.com/james-cook-university-wins-appeal-against-professor-peter-ridd/|title=James Cook University wins appeal against Professor Peter Ridd|date= 25 July 2020|access-date= 15 October 2021|work=Sterling Law}}</ref> Ridd appealed to the [[High Court of Australia]], but that appeal was dismissed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sterlinglawqld.com/peter-ridd-loses-high-court-appeal/|title=Peter Ridd loses High Court appeal|date= 13 October 2021|access-date= 15 October 2021|work=Sterling Law}}</ref><ref name="hca">{{Citation|title=Ridd v James Cook University|date=2021-10-13|url=http://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/cases/cth/HCA//2021/32.html|issue=32|access-date=2021-10-21}}</ref>
